title: Optimal additive error of linear-size spanners
formal: Determine the optimal worst-case additive error \(A_c(n)\) of a spanner with at most \(\lfloor cn\rfloor\) edges, up to multiplicative constant factors as \(n\to\infty\), for every fixed real constant \(c\geq1\). The graph is arbitrary, undirected and unweighted; the edge budget is genuinely linear, without hidden factors depending on \(n\).
why: The linear edge regime compresses a graph to a constant number of retained edges per vertex. Determining its unavoidable distance loss would quantify a fundamental limit on how accurately arbitrary graph metrics can survive such strong sparsification.
status_note: The survey leaves the linear-size error tradeoff open. The later lower-bound and nearly linear upper-bound abstracts were checked on 13 September 2026 and do not give matching bounds for every fixed linear coefficient. No full determination was verified; status remains source_open.
review_note: Completed individual source and formulation review on 13 September 2026; see statement_review and research/card-completion-20260913/reviews.jsonl.

progress.text: The survey explicitly asks for the optimal additive error achievable with a linear number of edges.
The later paper proves an \(\Omega(n^{1/7})\) lower bound in the linear-edge regime.
The subsequent upper-bound abstract reports \(O(n^{0.403})\) error with \(\widetilde O(n)\) edges, a distinct edge budget from the strict linear target.

importance.reason: The general additive-distance loss forced by a linear edge budget is a central sparsity-versus-accuracy question for graph metrics.

sentences: A linear-size spanner retains only a constant number of edges per vertex on average.
For arbitrary graphs, this severe sparsity budget can force shortest paths to become longer.
The source asks for the smallest additive error that can always be guaranteed under that budget.
The error may grow with graph size, unlike a fixed additive approximation target.
The project seeks matching constructions and lower bounds describing the exact amount of metric accuracy necessarily lost when a graph is compressed to linear edge count.

definitions: For every \(n\geq1\), let \(\mathcal G_n\) be the finite set of simple undirected graphs on \([n]\). Every edge has length one. A spanning subgraph \(H\subseteq G\) has the same vertices, retains only original edges, and must have the same connected components as \(G\). There are no Steiner vertices, shortcut edges or changed edge lengths. Let \[\Delta(G,H)=\max_{u,v:\,d_G(u,v)<\infty}\bigl(d_H(u,v)-d_G(u,v)\bigr),\qquad A_c(n)=\max_{G\in\mathcal G_n}\min_{\substack{H\subseteq G,\ |E(H)|\leq\lfloor cn\rfloor\\ H\text{ preserves components}}}\Delta(G,H).\] Distances count edges. Pairs with \(u=v\) are included, so the maximum is defined and nonnegative even in an edgeless graph. A spanning forest is feasible for \(c\geq1\); thus the quantity is finite. A result up to constant factors supplies a nonnegative function \(a(n,c)\) and, for each fixed \(c\), constants \(0<L_c\leq U_c<\infty\) and \(n_c\) with \(L_c a(n,c)\leq A_c(n)\leq U_c a(n,c)\) for every \(n\geq n_c\). Constants may depend on \(c\), never on \(n\). This measures optimal structural approximation, not the running time for finding a spanner; no algorithmic cost bound is imposed. The explicit coefficient \(c\) makes the source’s unspecified linear-size constant a parameter of the target.

context_blocks.text: The survey’s Section 8.4, item 3, asks how much additive error is unavoidable with \(O(n)\) retained edges. Its dated bounds leave a polynomial gap between what sparse subgraphs can achieve and what some input metrics force.

Bodwin and Hoppenworth subsequently establish an \(\Omega(n^{1/7})\) additive-error lower bound for linear-size spanners, improving the lower bound quoted in the survey. This is a lower bound, not a matching determination.

The later Almost-Optimal Sublinear Additive Spanners abstract reports \(O(n^{0.403})\) additive error with \(\widetilde O(n)\) edges. That edge budget hides logarithmic factors and cannot be substituted for a fixed \(cn\) budget in this question.

answer_criterion: Supply a complete Lean-checked asymptotic determination of the defined family, with matching upper and lower bounds up to multiplicative constants for every fixed edge coefficient. The upper bound must cover every input graph and the lower bound must establish matching worst cases under the same edge budget. Determining only an exponent with an unresolved polynomial or logarithmic gap does not meet this precision; a numerical tolerance of 1/100 is not an additive error on asymptotic notation.
